name: Culver Cadet
variants: PQ-8 / PQ-8A / PQ-14 radio-controlled target drones (some with fixed tricycle gear)
summary: Small pre-war two-seat low-wing designed by Al Mooney, also mass-produced as a radio-controlled target drone in WWII. Retractable main gear was unusual on such a small plane.

wings: Low cantilever wing with no struts
engines: Single small flat-four (75-90 hp) in a neat cowl
fuselage: Smooth semi-monocoque fuselage with a long, rounded canopy over two seats
Retractable main gear with a tailwheel (drone versions fixed tricycle)

tellTales: Tiny low-wing two-seater whose main wheels fold away yet sits on a tailwheel
Smooth enclosed cabin with a rounded glassy canopy line
No struts anywhere on a small prewar airframe

confusedWith.howToTell: The Culver V is a postwar successor with retractable tricycle gear and outer wing panels that angle upward; the Cadet has a tailwheel and a more conventional wing.
The Dart G is the earlier fixed-gear tube-and-fabric ancestor; the Cadet has a smoother metal fuselage and retractable main gear.
The Swift is a postwar all-metal two-seater with a tall swept fin and slender fuselage; the Cadet is a prewar design with a more conventional, rounder fuselage.
The Mite is a tiny single-seater on retractable tricycle gear; the Cadet has two seats and a tailwheel.
